ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Macro-level dominance of high-intensity (white) pixels occupying approximately 70-75% of the central surface area, sharply contrasted by low-intensity (black) pixels at the trailing edges and peduncle insertion.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white regions occupy the central-left and central-right lobes. Low-intensity black bands define the perimeter, with significant mottling and focal black spots scattered throughout the white field, particularly a large cluster around the median notch and a distinct circular spot on the right lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with an estimated internal pixel angle of approximately 75 degrees.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serrations (sawtooth pattern) are visible along the distal trailing edge of the right lobe; the left lobe displays lower-frequency, undulating peaks of varying pixel height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curvature along the superior leading edges transitioning to a concave sweep on the trailing edges near the notch, straightening toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Massive clusters of high-contrast, multi-tonal (beige and white) pixels indicating heavy barnacle colonization localized at the extreme lateral tips of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple low-intensity (black) unaligned linear vectors, resembling rake marks, traversing the high-intensity white zones on both lobes, with higher density on the right medial lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive distal tip trauma characterized by heavy barnacle encrustation and distinct linear scarring/rake marks across the ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: A singular, isolated circular black pixel cluster (spot) located in the mid-white region of the right fluke lobe.
